facts.text: Suminoe‑ku keeps Taisho‑era shipbuilding alive, with rusting docks and old wood‑frame homes left intact, creating a layered time‑capsule landscape.
The Osaka Maritime Museum, designed by Paul Andreu, won awards before closing in 2013 after just a decade of operation.
Osaka Nanko Bird Sanctuary spans 19 hectares, welcoming migratory birds from Siberia and New Zealand each spring.
Chidori Bunka, a community arts complex, occupies a cluster of old interconnected buildings that now house galleries, workshops, and studios.
Creative Center Osaka, a dockside arts and performance complex, attracts indie artists, urban farms, and underground music venues.
Despite its name, Suminoe’s historic park lies across the border inside Suminoe‑ku, not in Sumiyoshi‑ku.
